texts.li: [theirLowtech] Since the {FACTION} visitors came, {X_nameDef} has split most of the colony's firewood, always at the block next to {A_nameDef}'s. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked whether the colony would keep {X_objective} when {X_possessive} people go.\n\nThe {FACTION} elders won't like losing a pair of hands. {A_nameDef} is trying not to look hopeful.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came to the council with questions, as practical as a trader's: where {X_pronoun} would sleep if {X_pronoun} stayed on, and whether the bunk next to {A_nameDef}'s is taken. The rest of the visitors leave in the morning.\n\n{FACTION} keeps count of its people and won't be glad to lose one.

[winter] The {FACTION} visitors go back out into the snow tomorrow, without {X_nameDef} if {X_pronoun} has any say in it. {X_nameDef} has spent most of the visit at {A_nameDef}'s side and asks to stay the winter, and longer if the colony will have {X_objective}.\n\n{FACTION} will want {X_objective} back.

[colony:Open] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} heard on the road that this colony takes people in, and has spent the visit finding out if it's true, mostly from {A_nameDef}. Now {X_nameDef} has asked to stay when the others go, and {A_nameDef} has already found {X_objective} a spare blanket.\n\n{FACTION} will count it as a loss.

[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has shown {X_nameDef} everything worth seeing in the colony, down to the spot on the wall where the sunset is best. Now {X_nameDef} wants to stay when the {FACTION} party goes, and {A_nameDef} is standing next to {X_objective} at the council table.\n\n{FACTION} won't thank the colony for it.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} carried {X_possessive} pack inside before the council could change its mind. Whoever speaks for {FACTION} wouldn't shake hands on the way out.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} slept under the colony's roof that night. The {FACTION} people struck camp before light, and their elders will hear of it.
The council paid {FACTION} two hundred silver, and {X_nameDef} stayed. {A_nameDef} helped {X_objective} carry {X_possessive} things in.
[winter] {X_nameDef} left with {FACTION} into the snow. {A_nameDef} stood at the gate until they were out of sight.
{X_nameDef} went with {FACTION} in the morning, and looked back twice before the road turned. {A_nameDef} didn't touch breakfast.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has called {A_nameDef} a dirt-eater twice today, once at the well and once at supper, and laughed both times. The other visitors have started laughing along.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council whether a guest's tongue is the council's business.

[theirHightech] Today {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef}, slowly and loudly, whether {A_pronoun} could read. It capped two days of remarks about the colony's beds and the colony's smell, most of them aimed at {A_nameDef}.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to say something.

[trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} took against each other at first sight, and both have said so. Today {X_nameDef} went further, and said something about {A_nameDef}'s family that stopped all talk at the table.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to act. Several people think {A_nameDef} started it.

[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has put up with {X_nameDef}'s remarks for two days without a word back. Tonight {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} made {A_nameDef} leave the dinner table in tears, and some of the others want the council to act even though {A_nameDef} won't ask.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} apologized to {A_nameDef} at supper, through {X_possessive} teeth. {A_nameDef} accepted it, and passed the bread.
[trait:Kind] The council let it go. {A_nameDef} said nothing more about it and kept away from the visitors until they left.
The council said nothing. {X_nameDef} found new things to say about {A_nameDef} every day of the visit.
[theirLowtech] The {FACTION} visitors rolled up their bedding and went. {X_nameDef} found something to shout back at the colony from every rise in the road.

texts.li: [theirHightech] {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, already has a buyer in mind for the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries, a collector in a city {A_nameDef} has never heard of, and named a price on the spot. It's good silver.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been holding the thing in both hands since the trader asked.

[colony:Traditional] The colony keeps its dead's things, mostly. {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, has made a good offer for the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries anyway, and {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether {A_pronoun} may say yes.

[trait:Greedy] {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, offered silver for the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries, and {A_nameDef} said yes before the sentence was finished. Then {A_nameDef} remembered whose it had been, and asked the council to decide instead.

lines.li: [trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} sold it for {COUNT} silver and spent the evening counting it. The next morning {A_nameDef} went out to the graves before breakfast.
The heirloom stays. {A_nameDef} has been polishing it since the trader left.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} has been singing to {A_nameDef} through the cell door, songs from the {FACTION} villages about harvests and homecomings. Tonight {X_nameDef} stopped singing long enough to ask to be sent home, and {A_nameDef} brought the request straight to the council.

[winter] It's cold in the cells, and {X_nameDef} has been telling {A_nameDef} about the people of {FACTION} who'll go hungry this winter without {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to let {X_nameDef} go home before the snow gets deeper.

[x:old] {X_nameDef} is too old to have been raiding, {A_nameDef} says, and was only carrying water for the others. {X_nameDef} wants to go home to {FACTION} and see {X_possessive} grandchildren, and {A_nameDef} wants the council to let {X_objective}.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} walked out of the gate with a loaf of bread and {A_nameDef}'s second-best coat. {FACTION} will hear about it.
{A_nameDef} sat by the door and let {X_nameDef} talk. Near the end, {X_nameDef} was asking about the colony instead of about home.
{X_nameDef} stopped talking through the door after that.

texts.li: [winter] One of the {FACTION} attackers is still alive out in the snow: {X_nameDef}, bleeding and too cold to shout anymore. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} and came straight to the council.\n\nIn this cold, {X_nameDef} won't last the afternoon.

[night] It's dark, and somewhere past the wall one of the {FACTION} attackers is calling for help. {A_nameDef} went out with a light, found {X_nameDef} alive and bleeding, and came back to ask what to do.

[x:old] Among the fallen {FACTION} attackers is {X_nameDef}, gray-haired and badly hurt, who keeps asking {A_nameDef} whether the others got away.\n\n{X_nameDef} is too old to be raiding, and too hurt to wait long for an answer.

[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} is kneeling next to {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} attackers, pressing a rag to the wound and calling for the council to decide. An hour ago {X_nameDef} was trying to kill {A_objective}.

[trait:Bloodlust] {A_nameDef} found {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} still breathing among the dead, and came back asking whether the council wants {X_objective} finished. Others would rather a prison bed.\n\n{X_nameDef} is bleeding while they argue.

[past:healer] {A_nameDef} has seen wounds like {X_nameDef}'s before and knows there isn't much time. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came at the colony with a weapon not an hour ago. Now {A_nameDef} wants the council to say whether to try and save {X_objective}.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} warriors, lies where {X_pronoun} fell with a broken spear beside {X_objective}, asking {A_nameDef} for water in {X_possessive} own tongue. {A_nameDef} understood that much.

lines.li: {A_nameDef} hauled {X_nameDef} up over one shoulder and went looking for a prison bed.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} carried {X_nameDef} in, still pressing the rag to the wound, and asked who had a prison bed made up.
[winter] {A_nameDef} wrapped {X_nameDef} in a spare coat and dragged {X_objective} through the snow toward the prison beds.
[trait:Bloodlust] {A_nameDef} made it quick, and wiped the blade on {X_nameDef}'s coat.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} held {X_nameDef}'s hand and made it quick, then sat a while before coming back in.
[winter] The council left {X_nameDef} to the cold. By evening the snow had covered {X_objective}.
[night] In the dark, {X_nameDef} called for help, then for someone by name, then not at all.

texts.li: [winter] {X_nameDef} and a few others of {FACTION} came through the snow to ask for food. Their stores froze and split, and they've been eating their seed since the first frost. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} at the gate, plainly, with no speech prepared.

[theirLowtech] Blight got the {FACTION} fields this year. {X_nameDef} has walked two days with an empty basket to ask the colony for whatever it can spare, and {A_nameDef} has brought the request to the council.
[colony:Generous] The colony has a name for giving, and the name has carried. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate with empty sacks, asking {A_nameDef} for food for the people back home.

[colony:Thrifty] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard the colony doesn't give much away, and came anyway. Their stores are empty. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for food at the gate and waited for the answer with {X_possessive} hat in {X_possessive} hands.

[x:old] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is old and bent nearly double under an empty sack, and has walked a long way to ask for food for the young ones back home. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} resting at the gate.

lines.li: [winter] They left with full sacks on their backs, bent under the weight, back into the snow. {X_nameDef} said {FACTION} would remember.
The sacks were filled from the colony's own stores. {X_nameDef} shook {A_nameDef}'s hand for a long time before leaving.
[winter] The {FACTION} people waited at the gate until dark, then went back out into the snow.

texts.li: [rain] {PET_nameDef} has been in a foul mood all day in the rain, and when {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} reached down to pat {PET_objective}, {PET_nameDef} bit. {X_nameDef} wants silver for it. {A_nameDef} says {PET_nameDef} would have bitten {A_objective} too, in that weather.

[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has already bandaged {X_nameDef}'s hand and apologized three times for {PET_nameDef}. It isn't enough: the {FACTION} visitors want silver for the bite, and a few of them want the animal.

[night] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} went for a walk after dark and tripped over {PET_nameDef}, asleep by the door. {PET_nameDef} bit first and woke up after. The {FACTION} visitors want silver for it, and {A_nameDef} wants to know what a guest was doing creeping around in the dark.

lines.li: {PET_nameDef} stays, unpunished. {A_nameDef} took {PET_objective} for a long walk, well away from the visitors.

texts.li: [winter] Hunger has brought {X_indefinite} down close to the colony. {A_nameDef} found its den under the snow, not far from the storeroom. It hasn't attacked anyone yet.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks a hungry animal can be won over with a bucket of meat. Others think it should be killed before it gets hungrier.

[night] {A_nameDef} heard something circling the storeroom in the dark, and followed the tracks this morning to a den in the brush, where {X_indefinite} lay watching {A_objective} come.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants to tame it. Others want it gone, one way or another.

[b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} has already been out to look at the den {A_nameDef} found. There's {X_indefinite} in there, thin and wary, and {B_nameDef} came back saying it's only hungry.\n\nNot everyone is as sure as {B_nameDef}.

lines.li: {B_nameDef} has been leaving meat outside the den every evening. The others have been told to keep to the paths and not to run.

texts.li: [rain] {A_nameDef} came in soaked, carrying {X_indefinite} wrapped in {A_possessive} coat, and announced that it was cold and lost and had no one. {A_nameDef} wants to keep it.\n\nThe adults can see how this is going to go.

[spring] {A_nameDef} found {X_indefinite} in the long grass this morning, small enough to fit in two hands, and hasn't put it down since. {A_nameDef} wants to keep it, and has already made it a bed in a crate.

[snow] All week {A_nameDef} has been sneaking bread to {X_indefinite} sheltering from the snow under the porch. Today {A_nameDef} asked the council, very politely, whether it could come inside for good.

lines.li: {A_nameDef} took the answer to the storeroom and cried there, loudly enough to be heard from the kitchen.

texts.li: [!lowtech] {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} today whether the colony had heard of insulation, and then whether it had heard of architects. {A_nameDef} built the guest room {X_nameDef} sleeps in.\n\nA titled guest is good for the colony's standing. {A_nameDef} wants to know if it's worth this.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} told the table at supper that in the capital even the stables have straight walls. {A_nameDef}, who raised most of the walls here, put down {A_possessive} cup and asked the council what it means to do about its guest.

[winter] {X_nameDef} has complained of a draft in the guest room every morning this week, and this morning said the draft was the only thing in the colony built with any skill. {A_nameDef} built the room.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to say something to its guest.

lines.li: [trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} what a title is worth out here, with examples. {X_nameDef} left the table, and {FACTION} will hear about it.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} sells a tonic in clay jars, brewed from marsh roots by somebody's grandmother. It cures bad sleep, bad joints and bad luck, and the last jar costs one hundred silver.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been sleeping badly for weeks, and wants it.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef}'s tonic comes in a sealed glass vial with a printed label, and the label promises a great deal. {X_nameDef} wants one hundred silver for it. {A_nameDef}, who hasn't slept properly in weeks, has read the label four times.

[trait:Nervous] {A_nameDef} has been jumpy for days and sleeping worse each night. {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, noticed, and has a tonic for exactly that: one hundred silver for the bottle.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to buy it.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} packed the tonic away and moved on to selling buttons. {A_nameDef} lay awake that night, wondering.

texts.li: [past:outlaw] {X_nameDef} rode with {A_nameDef} once, back when {A_nameDef} lived outside the law, and recognized {A_objective} across the {FACTION} camp. {X_nameDef} knows the worst of it ({SECRET}).\n\nFor one hundred and fifty silver, {X_nameDef} will forget. {A_nameDef} told the council all of this in a flat voice, looking at the table.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knew {A_nameDef} in another valley, under another name, and knows why {A_nameDef} left it ({SECRET}). {X_nameDef} has suggested, pleasantly, that one hundred and fifty silver would help {X_objective} forget.

lines.li: The council wouldn't pay. {X_nameDef} told the story at supper, slowly, so it would last.

texts.li: [night] Eyes in the dark past the fields, low to the ground. {A_nameDef} knew them. They belong to {X_definite}, the beast that mauled one of the colonists and got away, and it hasn't forgotten the way here.

[winter] {A_nameDef} found tracks in the snow this morning, circling the colony twice. They belong to {X_definite}, the animal that mauled a colonist and limped off into the wild.\n\nThe winter has made it bolder.

lines.li: The doors stay barred until {X_definite} moves on. There have already been two arguments over the same chair.

texts.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has carried {X_nameDef}'s meals down to the cell every day, though {X_nameDef} is the one who hurt {A_objective}. Today {A_nameDef} came back up shaking, and asked the council to decide what {X_nameDef} is to the colony now.

[trait:Bloodlust] {A_nameDef} has been sharpening a blade outside {X_nameDef}'s cell door, slowly, so {X_nameDef} can hear. {X_nameDef} is the one who hurt {A_nameDef} and got away, and now the colony feeds {X_objective}.\n\nThe council has to decide what happens to this prisoner before {A_nameDef} decides for it.

lines.li: The cell door stays shut. {A_nameDef} has asked someone else to carry the meals down.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has looked at {PET_nameDef}'s teeth, felt {PET_possessive} legs and walked around {PET_objective} twice, the way people buy animals at a fair. The offer is one hundred and twenty silver.\n\n{A_nameDef} hasn't let go of the lead.

[colony:Thrifty] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has offered one hundred and twenty silver for {PET_nameDef}, having heard the colony likes a good price. {A_nameDef} has heard the same, and is watching the council very carefully.

lines.li: Not for sale. {A_nameDef} gave {PET_definite} the rest of {A_possessive} supper that night.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef}, a bone-setter traveling with {FACTION}, watched {A_nameDef} limp across the yard and offered to see to the old injury for eighty silver. {B_nameDef}, who does the colony's doctoring, wants to watch and learn, and thinks {B_pronoun} could probably do as well.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} carries a proper medical kit and a certificate {X_pronoun} shows to anyone who asks. For eighty silver {X_nameDef} will look at {A_nameDef}'s old injury. {B_nameDef}, who does most of the colony's doctoring, wants to watch closely.

lines.li: {B_nameDef} has promised {A_nameDef} a proper look at the old injury, when there's time.
